name: Pulmonary Artery Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of underdeveloped pulmonary artery on angiography or CT/MRI
Presence of pulmonary hypertension confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary artery stenosis or hypoplasia such as acquired vascular disease or external compression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic confirmation of pulmonary artery hypoplasia plus evidence of pulmonary hypertension with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and hemodynamic assessment; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features are present.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected on physical examination or imaging
searchTerms: reduced pulse in one lung artery
diminished blood flow pulse in lung

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced perfusion of affected lung on ventilation-perfusion scan
searchTerms: poor blood flow to lung on scan
low blood supply in affected lung
lack of energy from decreased oxygen

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure

rare.symptomName: Right ventricular hypertrophy detected on ECG
searchTerms: enlarged right heart muscle on ECG
right ventricular thickening on heart tracing
ECG signs of right heart enlargement

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in cases with right heart strain
imaging: Chest X-ray showing decreased vascular markings on affected side
CT angiography demonstrating hypoplastic pulmonary artery
Echocardiography indicating pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular hypertrophy
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be associated with congenital syndromes involving vascular development
other: Cardiac catheterization confirming pulmonary artery pressures and anatomy

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary artery stenosis involves localized narrowing rather than diffuse hypoplasia
Complete absence of pulmonary artery rather than hypoplastic vessel
Imaging shows absence rather than underdevelopment
Imaging shows organized thrombi and vascular obstruction

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Signs of right heart failure (jugular venous distension, peripheral edema)
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016 Jan 1;37(1):67-119.
Muthialu N, et al. Pulmonary artery hypoplasia: clinical features and management. Ann Pediatr Cardiol. 2018;11(3):234-240.
